messages:
irene: Quick RFC follow-up — I sketched a decomposed query surface for Console: intent layer (authz + routing) -> projection layer (view tiling + aggregation) -> render layer. Goal: make RBAC cheap and cacheable, reduce per-tenant cold KV cache thrash. Thoughts?

alex: +1 on separation. Main risk is added network hops and serialization cost between layers. do we want gRPC or in-process calls?

maria: We should be explicit about where RBAC lives. If authz stays in intent, projection can be cached across tenants? risky.

irene: Good call. Proposal: keep authz in intent, but emit a signed projection token bounded to tenant and query fingerprint. projection layer validates token and can safely reuse cached tiles. That avoids full RBAC checks inside projection.

sam: How do we sign/verify tokens? sync with KMS? latency concerns.

irene: Simple HMAC with per-cluster key initially. We can rotate keys monthly. Not meant to be crypto-heavy, just tamper-proof for cache safety.

alex: Will token approach break multi-tenant isolation for Dedicated customers who require full per-tenant keying?

irene: For Dedicated we can use per-tenant keys (config in tenant metadata service). For hosted default cluster key. So projection layer looks up key id in token header.

maria: OK. Operationally we need metrics: token validation latency, projection cache hit rate, token-mismatch rate. Also audit logs for token issuance.

sam: Another tradeoff: prefix cache (KV) vs full tile. If projection is too aggressive, we might serve stale tiles when RBAC changes (role removed). What's TTL plan?

irene: TTLs should be short for auth-sensitive tiles. Plan: 30s by default for role-sensitive panels, 10m for purely telemetry read-only tiles. We can tag tiles with sensitivity flags at compile time from panel descriptors.

alex: Rollout strategy? big bang is dangerous.

irene: Rollout plan I sketched:
1) Add intent/projection RPC interfaces (feature flag off)
2) Emit signed tokens in intent, but still call projection with full RBAC in 10% traffic (canary)
3) Gradually increase canary while monitoring: 95p latency, error rate, projection cache hit, audit mismatches
4) Flip default flag for new panels, run full traffic after 2 weeks of stable metrics

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment triggered: console-query-v2 on us-east-1 cluster at 2024-10-03T14:22:00Z.

maria: We need a migration checklist item: ensure evals (prompt sets) for dashboard queries exist so we can detect quality regressions after projection caching.

sam: Also add a guard: if token validation fails or sensitivity flag set, fall back to full RBAC check and mark tile non-cacheable for a short duration. That should keep correctness.

irene: Exactly. I'll draft an RFC addendum with the token format, projected interfaces, and a concise rollout checklist. Quick pseudo-config example for feature flags:

```
feature_flags:
  console_query_v2: {
    enabled: false,
    canary_percent: 10,
    rollout_metrics: ["projection_cache_hit","intent_latency_95","rbac_fallback_rate"]
  }
```

alex: Sounds solid. Please include a follow-up section on observability queries (how to compute projection cache hit from our telemetry tables).

maria: I'll pair on that. Also adding owners for key rotation: security + infra.

irene: Thanks — I'll put the addendum in the RFC repo and ping this thread when ready.

sam: quick nit: add a cleanup job for stale token keys in projection cache to prevent unbounded memory growth.

irene: noted. I'll add it.

ops-bot: reminder: RFC-1247 (Console Query Decomp) awaiting addendum PR.
